pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📊 **Strand 4 — Handling Data**
Collecting, organising, presenting and interpreting information to make good decisions.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B8.4.1)
- B8.4.1.2 — Demonstrate understanding of the measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and range, and explain when it is most appropriate to use the mean, median or mode.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- calculate the mean, median and mode of ungrouped data (lists, tables and bar graphs)
- explain why the three measures may be the same or different
- justify which measure best represents a set of data in a given context

lessons.title: Calculating the mean, median and mode

pages.title: Calculating the mean, median and mode
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Calculate the mean, median and mode for a given set of ungrouped data, and explain why these values may be the same or different.
Curriculum indicator B8.4.1.2.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: The three averages** — **Mean** = sum of values ÷ number of values. **Median** = middle value of the ordered data. **Mode** = the value that occurs most often (there may be more than one mode, or none). **Range** = highest value − lowest value (a measure of spread).
## ✏️ Example 14.1
The bar graph shows a small business's sales from Monday to Friday. Calculate the mean, median and mode, and explain your findings.
[[fig:m8-f50]]
Figure 14.1: Daily sales collected (GH₵)
**Solution**
Sales: Mon 150, Tue 100, Wed 150, Thu 200, Fri 150.
Mean = [[150 + 100 + 150 + 200 + 150/5]] = [[750/5]] = **GH₵150**
Ordered: 100, 150, **150**, 150, 200 → Median = **GH₵150**
Mode = **GH₵150** (three times)
All three are the same because the data are **symmetrical**: the values below 150 (100) and above 150 (200) are the same distance from 150, and 150 is in the middle and most common.

pages.title: Example 14.2
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 14.2
The table shows the floor area of the sitting rooms of 7 houses (A to G) in Kwashiman.
| **House** | **A** | **B** | **C** | **D** | **E** | **F** | **G** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Area (m²) | 22 | 24 | 26 | 30 | 48 | 30 | 30 |
a) Work out the mean, median and mode. b) Draw a bar chart. c) Explain why the values are the same.
**Solution**
a) Mean = [[22 + 24 + 26 + 30 + 48 + 30 + 30/7]] = [[210/7]] = **30 m²**. Ordered: 22, 24, 26, **30**, 30, 30, 48 → median = **30 m²**. Mode = **30 m²**.
b)
[[fig:m8-f51]]
Figure 14.2: Sitting room floor areas
c) The large value 48 (18 above 30) is balanced by the three smaller values 22, 24 and 26 (8 + 6 + 4 = 18 below 30), so the mean is still 30, which is also the middle and the most frequent value.
## ✏️ Example 14.3
The table and bar graph show how often each data value from 1 to 7 occurs.
| **Data value** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** | **6** | **7** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 1 | 11 | 5 | 4 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
a) Calculate the mean, median and mode. b) Locate them on the graph. c) Explain why they are different.
**Solution**
a) Σf = 25; Σfx = 1 + 22 + 15 + 16 + 10 + 6 + 7 = 77. **Mean =** [[77/25]] **= 3.08**.
The median is the 13th value. Cumulative frequencies: 1, 12, 17, … so the 13th value is **3**. The mode is **2** (frequency 11).
[[fig:m8-f52]]
Figure 14.3: Mode, median and mean marked on the graph
c) The data are **not symmetrical** — they are bunched at 2 with a long "tail" of larger values (4 to 7). The tail pulls the mean up above the median, and the median is above the mode: **mode < median < mean**.

pages.title: Exercise 14.1
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 14.1** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Find the mean, median, mode and range of: a) 7, 3, 9, 3, 5, 8, 3, 10 b) 15, 18, 15, 20, 22, 18, 15
2. The table shows the number of goals scored in 30 matches. Find the mean, median and mode.
| **Goals** | **0** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matches | 6 | 9 | 7 | 4 | 3 | 1 |
3. Find a set of five numbers whose mean, median and mode are all 6.
4. Explain why, for the data 2, 3, 3, 4, 38, the mean is much larger than the median.

questions.q: Find the mean, median, mode and range of:

The table shows the number of goals scored in 30 matches. Find the mean, median and mode.
| **Goals** | **0** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matches | 6 | 9 | 7 | 4 | 3 | 1 |

parts.a: Mean = 52 ÷ 30 ≈ 1.73; median = 1.5 (15th and 16th values are 1 and 2); mode = 1

questions.q: Find a set of five numbers whose mean, median and mode are all 6.
Explain why, for the data 2, 3, 3, 4, 38, the mean is much larger than the median.

parts.a: The extreme value (outlier) 38 increases the sum a lot, pulling the mean (10) up, but it does not change the middle value (3).

pages.title: Choosing the best measure
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Justify a context in which the mean, median or mode is the most appropriate measure of central tendency to use when reporting findings.
Curriculum indicator B8.4.1.2.2
| **Measure** | **Best used when …** | **Weakness** |
|---|---|---|
| Mean | data are fairly symmetrical with no extreme values; every value should count (e.g. average test mark) | strongly affected by extreme values (outliers) |
| Median | data contain extreme values or are skewed (e.g. salaries, house prices) | ignores the actual sizes of most values |
| Mode | data are categorical, or we want the most common value (e.g. shoe size to stock, favourite colour) | may not exist or may not be central |
## ✏️ Example 14.4
Kojo's taxi makes these numbers of trips each day:
| **Day** | **Mon** | **Tue** | **Wed** | **Thu** | **Fri** | **Sat** | **Sun** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trips | 8 | 6 | 10 | 10 | 9 | 10 | 3 |
a) Calculate the mean, median and mode. b) Which measure best represents the number of trips Kojo makes each day? c) Justify your choice.
**Solution**
a) Mean = [[56/7]] = **8**. Ordered: 3, 6, 8, **9**, 10, 10, 10 → median = **9**. Mode = **10**.
b) The **median (9)** is the best choice (the mean, 8, is also acceptable).
c) Sunday's 3 trips is unusually low (perhaps Kojo rests or goes to church) and pulls the mean down to 8, which is lower than on 5 of the 7 days. The mode (10) happens on only 3 days and overstates a typical day. The median, 9, is in the middle of the data and is not affected by the unusual Sunday value.

pages.title: Exercise 14.2
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 14.2** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Which average would you use? Explain. a) A shoe seller deciding which size to order most of. b) The typical salary in a company where the manager earns GH₵30,000 and ten workers earn about GH₵2,000. c) The average mark in a class test where marks range from 40 to 75.
2. The monthly incomes (GH₵) of 7 workers are 1,800, 2,100, 1,950, 2,000, 15,000, 1,900, 2,050. Find the mean and median. Which better describes a typical income?

questions.q: Which average would you use? Explain.

parts.q: (a) A shoe seller deciding which size to order most of.
(b) The typical salary in a company where the manager earns GH₵30,000 and ten workers earn about GH₵2,000.
parts.a: Median — the manager's salary is an extreme value

parts.q: (c) The average mark in a class test where marks range from 40 to 75.
parts.a: Mean — there are no extreme values

questions.q: The monthly incomes (GH₵) of 7 workers are 1,800, 2,100, 1,950, 2,000, 15,000, 1,900, 2,050. Find the mean and median. Which better describes a typical income?

parts.a: Mean ≈ GH₵3,828.57; median = GH₵2,000. The median is more typical; the mean is pulled up by the GH₵15,000 income.

pages.title: Chapter 14 summary
pages.body:
- Mean, median and mode are equal when data are symmetrical; they differ when data are skewed or have extreme values.
- Mean: uses all data, affected by outliers. Median: not affected by outliers. Mode: most common; works for categories.

questions.q: Find the mean, median, mode and range of 12, 15, 11, 15, 18, 13, 15, 21.
The mean of 8 numbers is 14. When one number is removed the mean becomes 13. What number was removed? ___
Five learners have a mean age of 13 years and a median age of 13 years. The modal age is 12 years. Write down a possible set of ages.
A football coach says, "Our average is 2 goals per match." The goals were 0, 1, 0, 9, 1, 1, 2. Which average did he use? Is it a fair summary? Explain.

parts.a: The mean (14 ÷ 7 = 2). Not fair — the single 9-goal match inflates it; the median and mode (both 1) are more typical.
